2.text: which work on the same principle as the wooden ones. Sometimes, in the

3.text: deep snow among the rough ice, a pit is dug and covered with a large block

4.text: of ice. This is well poised on its axis, and will swing on slight pressure; so

5.text: that the animal stepping on it falls into the pit, and the ice-block comes to

6.text: its former place by its own weight.

7.text: Strychnine pills, procured from Russian or American traders, and wrapped

8.text: in blubber or tallow, are also occasionally used for killing animals.

9.text: The self-acting bow was probably copied from the Russians, together

10.text: with the sinew spring-trap. At the present time, of all the tribes of north-

11.text: eastern Asia, the Yakut and the Lamut use it most frequently. They secure

12.text: with it even elk and reindeer. The Chukchee employ it for small animals,

28.text: out of reach of foxes; or they were laid in a hole in the ice and water was poured

29.text: over them, so that it would freeze to a transparent protecting cover strong

30.text: enough to resist the attacks of smaller animals. The wolf would break through

31.text: the ice and swallow all the spits, which would unfold in the stomach, and,

32.text: breaking through its walls, cause the speedy death of the animal. But with

33.text: only one or two spits it was able to walk away for a considerable distance,

34.text: even so far that it would never be found by the hunter.

39.text: Chukchee and the Koryak are very fond of this mushroom; and when they find it in the woods, they pick it

40.text: off just as eagerly as the wolves snatch after the greased whalebone spits. The Chukchee believe, moreover,

41.text: that mice, when gathering roots for the winter, bring in some unknown intoxicating herbs which they use in

42.text: their ceremonials. These herbs also serve to protect their stores from intruders, because they are said to act

43.text: as poison on most other animals, including man. These herbs are called by a name derived from that of the
